name: TV DIABLO Windows
note: v2181: v2180 found the supervisor pause flag dated August 3 on his machine, read it as a forgotten leftover from a scan, and gave it a six hour expiry so it would clear itself. Then I read tvd-console.sh, the script whose entire job is clearing that flag, and it refuses by default and says exactly why: the console it restores is HEADLESS, a headless launch does not hold the macOS Screen Recording grant, so ON AIR refuses, nothing records, Theatre plays black, and on 2026-08-03 that cost a night of farming footage. That is the date on the flag. It is not forgotten, it is deliberate, and it is the only thing standing between the supervisor and putting a console on port 17772 that cannot record. My expiry would have re-caused that exact incident unattended, six hours after any scan, on a machine where nobody was watching. The same script already says that no tty is not consent, and a timer is a worse version of the consent this system deliberately requires. The expiry is removed and a guard now refuses to let it come back, carrying the reason with it so the next reader does not repeat what I did. What survives from v2180 is the half that was genuinely missing: the supervisor announces that it has stood down, how old the flag is, and why the flag is there, because a supervisor that is not supervising and does not say so is indistinguishable from one that is. The general lesson is the CrossOver one. Ask what a thing DOES before removing it, never what it looks like it costs.
